there is no one-size-fits-all solution to improve learning.

, in order to improve learning outcomes, we need to improve teaching quality and teacher accountability, and that the most promising approaches to do so are pedagogical and accountability interventions, and that we have not yet seen conclusive evidence for the efficacy of other approaches.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, despite their limitations, systematic reviews can be useful tools in the field of education, especially if they are conducted with an eye to the limitations of the research and are used to inform, rather than replace, the design and evaluation of education programs.

, in the absence of a comprehensive review that includes all relevant studies, the most useful way for policymakers to use systematic reviews to guide their decision-making is to consider a range of recommendations from different reviews, rather than relying on the results of any single review.
